newsitem.title: USA: Ammonia Hold tests biosolids composting.
newsitem.headline: Ammonia Hold tests biosolids composting.

text.p: Ammonia Hold Inc said Wednesday the recently completed first phase of a two-phase study demonstrated, on a research scale, that the addition of the Ammonia Hold product has the potential to accelerate the process of composting sludge.

The company, a manufacturer of odor-eliminating products for consumer and industrial markets, said it also showed the potential to accelerate the process of composting sludge, to increase the retention of nitrogen and to control the emission of ammonia during the composting process.
Ammonia Hold said it is beginning a phase-two commercial scale test of the product with various municipal sludge composting facilities. Test results should be available in 1997.

If the performance of Ammonia Hold is confirmed during phase-two performance testing, the product should be of particular interest to municipal wastewater treatment facilities that are considering or are currently composing sludge as a method of waste management, it said.

The company said the current use of sludge compost is estimated at 30 million tons per year, however, based on studies, the composting industry indicates a potential demand of 500 million tons per year.

The potential benefits of Ammonia Hold application to the treatment facilities are the reduction of composting cost and the control of air emissions and odor, with odor being the number one cause of complaints to health and environmental regulatory agencies.
